newsitem.title: FRANCE: Erap criticises Eramet over New Caledonia - paper.
newsitem.headline: Erap criticises Eramet over New Caledonia - paper.

text.p: The chairman of state holding Erap critised the way Eramet managers had handled a dispute over the distribution of mining assets in New Caledonia in a newspaper interview published on Wednesday.
"In this affair we blame Eramet's managers for having wasted an enormous amount of time," Erap chairman Remy Chardon told French daily La Tribune Desfosses.
Chardon, who became an Eramet board member on April 16, said Eramet's hard line had isolated the company from local authorities and parties in New Caledonia.
The company now had a "disastrous" image in New Caledonia due to the management's handling of the situation, Chardon said.
He said the government, Eramet's main shareholder, did not disagree with Eramet's development strategy but its tactics.
"There is disagreement over the way the issue was handled. And on how the company will get out of this situation," he said.

The goverment and Eramet are involved in a dispute over the distribution of mining assets in New Caledonia. The government wants to use some of Eramet's mining reserves to supply a rival plant that Canada's Falconbridge and local Kanak interests plan to build in the north of the island.
Eramet has said it does not oppose establishing a new plant as long as it did not threaten its own development in New Caledonia.
At last Thursday's board meeting, Erap said it wanted to appoint a majority of the directors on Eramet's board.
If shareholders approve the motion at the AGM on May 29, that could pave the way for the ousting of Eramet chairman Yves Rambaud, industry sources say.
"Erap would like to have an outright majority when Eramet's board is renewed," Chardon said. "The arrival of new men at the head of Eramet will help take some of the heat out of the conflict."
Eramet minority shareholders, notably pension funds, have been sharply critical of the government's role in the conflict.
Managers from Eramet, Falconbridge and Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) plan to meet in Paris on Friday to discuss plans to build the plant in the north.
Chardon said an agreement over mining assets was a priority but Eramet's management was in a difficult position to participate in future talks.
Eramet officials were not immediately available for comment.
